text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Sixty million voters cards have been printed by the electoral commission in readiness for compilation of voters register, sources at the commission said.
- Federal government to deduct from federation account 9.1 billion naira owed to banks by state governments so as to clear the debt, says chairman of national deposit insurance agency.
- Nigerian entrepreneurs rush for marginal oil wells which government is farming out for exploitation, say industry sources.
- Shrinking corporate earnings and low consumer purchasing power is forcing down share prices of many blue chip firms on the stock market, dealers say.
- Elf Nigeria unfolds plan to minimise gas flaring at its oil fields in the country.
- Ghana lifts a 1987 ban on importing drugs from Nigeria and other West African countries, according to directive issued by Ghana's health ministry to the country's pharmacy council.
- Court bars prominent lawyer Rotimi Williams from appearing for detained presidential claimant Moshood Abiola until the politician says he wants to change counsel.
- Managing director of Nigeria Airways Group Captain Peter Gana says the national carrier is seeking joint venture arrangements with foreign airlines.
- Dangote Group of companies owned by northern businessman Aliko Dangote acquires 40 percent of National Salt Company of Nigeria, the only salt refining company in West Africa.
